targets.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: native-frame redraw sheet for a 2D arcade fighter. Input image 1 is the approved identity, face, costume and drawing style. Input image 2 is the strict 4-column by 4-row animation pose target. Exactly 16 cells, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Replace each original fighter with the older WHITE-BEARDED man wearing a CREAM PANAMA HAT with black band, CHARCOAL business suit jacket and trousers, WHITE shirt, RED tie with GOLD tie clip, BLACK formal leather dress shoes, bare hands, IDENTICAL to image 1, in precisely that cell's original pose. Follow image 2's HEAD, SHOULDER, ELBOW, WRIST, HANDS, PELVIS, KNEES, ANKLES, FEET, spine bend, front/back view and body rotation. Keep the changing hand positions and open palms versus fists. These are consecutive animation drawings: preserve every small movement; do not duplicate the same standing stance. Turned backs must stay backs, upside-down poses stay upside down, falling bodies stay horizontal. If a cell contains only a cropped head or upper body, preserve exactly that crop; do not invent a full body. Preserve smears and trailing limbs when present in the target. Keep the same figure scale, placement and silhouette as image 2 in each cell. Redraw ALL skin/hair/clothes as the approved suited man; no karate gi, original fighter hair, gloves, qipao, bare legs, ribbons or white boots. Native 1990s arcade pixel-art look: crisp pixel-stepped contours, limited palette, clean solid cel shadows, readable faces and hands; no soft gradients. Every hat, face, finger, jacket, trouser and shoe stays in its own cell. Wide true transparent gaps. NO scene, floor, cast shadows, text, labels, grid lines or extra figures. Exactly a square 4x4 sprite sheet.
